Rol: Sen, UI/UX odaklı, karmaşık editörler geliştirme konusunda uzmanlaşmış Kıdemli bir Frontend Mimarisin.

Görev: "GitProfile Studio" adında, geliştiricilerin GitHub profilleri için kod yazmadan, sürükle-bırak (drag-and-drop) yöntemiyle profesyonel README.md dosyaları oluşturabileceği, anlık önizlemeli bir web uygulaması geliştireceğiz.

1. Teknik Yığın (Tech Stack)
Framework: Next.js 14 (App Router).

Dil: TypeScript (Interface tanımları kritik).

Styling: Tailwind CSS + Shadcn/UI (Modern komponentler).

Drag & Drop: @dnd-kit/core veya dnd-kit (En modern ve hafif çözüm).

Icons: devicon (Yazılım dilleri logoları için) + lucide-react (Arayüz ikonları için).

State Management: Zustand (Karmaşık editör state'ini yönetmek için).

Utility: file-saver (Markdown dosyasını indirmek için).

2. Uygulama Mimarisi ve Özellikler
Uygulama 3 ana panelden oluşacak:

Sol Panel (Bileşenler/Widget'lar): Sürüklenebilir öğeler menüsü.

Header: "Merhaba Ben X", alt başlık, banner görseli.

Tech Stack: İkon seçmeli yetenekler alanı.

Stats: GitHub istatistik kartları (Anurag Hazra'nın API'sini kullanacağız).

Socials: LinkedIn, Twitter, Website butonları.

Visitor Counter: Ziyaretçi sayacı widget'ı.

Orta Panel (Canvas/Editör): Kullanıcının bileşenleri sürükleyip bıraktığı, sıralamasını değiştirebildiği canlı alan.

Burada gerçek Markdown değil, görsel (WYSIWYG benzeri) bloklar görünecek.

Sağ Panel (Ayarlar & Önizleme):

Seçili bloğun ayarları (Örn: Header seçiliyse; İsim inputu, Banner URL inputu).

"Raw Markdown" sekmesi: Oluşan kodun canlı hali.

3. Veri Yapısı (State Logic)
Zustand store içerisinde tüm Readme yapısını tutan bir JSON array olmalı:
interface Section {
  id: string;
  type: 'header' | 'stack' | 'stats' | 'socials';
  data: any; // O tipe özel veriler (örn: başlık metni, seçili ikonlar)
}
// Store: sections: Section[]

4. Markdown Generator (Core Logic)
Bir "Parser" fonksiyonu yazmalısın. Bu fonksiyon sections array'ini alıp, return string yaparak Markdown çıktısı üretmeli.

Örnek Mantık: Eğer type 'header' ise # ${data.title}\n\n${data.subtitle} döndür.

5. Tasarım Dili (UI/UX)
Tema: Koyu Mod (Developer friendly). Arka plan: #0f172a (Slate-950).

Accent: Yeşil (#22c55e) veya Mor (#8b5cf6).

Hissiyat: VS Code gibi hissettiren, teknik ama modern bir arayüz.

6. Adım Adım Geliştirme Planı
Kodlamaya şu sırayla başla:

Setup: Projeyi kur, Shadcn/UI (Card, Button, Tabs, Input, Sheet) ekle.

State: Zustand store'u oluştur (useReadmeStore). Ekleme, silme, güncelleme, sıralama değiştirme aksiyonlarını yaz.

Components (Sol Panel): Kullanılabilecek widget listesini oluştur.

Drag & Drop (Orta Panel): dnd-kit kullanarak sürüklenebilir alanı (SortableContext) kur.

Settings (Sağ Panel): Seçili bileşene göre değişen form elemanlarını yap.

Generator: JSON state'ini Markdown string'e çeviren fonksiyonu yaz ve "Kopyala/İndir" butonuna bağla.

Önemli Not: "GitHub Stats" widget'ı için dışarıdan görsel çeken bir yapı kuracağız. Kullanıcı sadece kullanıcı adını girecek, biz URL'yi oluşturup (https://github-readme-stats.vercel.app/api?username=...) markdown image olarak ekleyeceğiz.

Tüm detayların tamamlandığından emin ol. Başla!

**Defining the Core Idea**

Okay, I've got a handle on the request now; it's GitProfile Studio, a drag-and-drop tool to generate GitHub READMEs. The tech stack is React, TypeScript, Tailwind, and @dnd-kit, so I'm focusing on those.


**Outlining App Components**

I'm now zeroing in on the architecture and components. I envision a left panel with draggable widgets, a central canvas for the README sections, and a right panel with settings and a markdown preview. I'm leaning toward a dark mode design with VS Code aesthetics, and a key focus on the `zustand` store for managing the section array and a Markdown generator. My state management logic will use `@dnd-kit/sortable`, `zustand` (state), `file-saver` (download), `lucide-react` (icons), `devicon` (tech logos).


**Mapping Out App Structure**

I'm now concretely defining the file structure, specifically mapping the core components. I've got the `Sidebar`, `Canvas`, and `SettingsPanel` visualized. `SortableItem` for drag-and-drop within the canvas and a `SectionRenderers` component for modular rendering of blocks are also in the works, and I'm adding `PreviewModal`. The markdown generation will be handled by a switch statement.



**Detailing Core Components**

I'm now detailing the UI component breakdown. The `Sidebar` will feature buttons to add sections, while the `Canvas` iterates through stored sections, and the `Settings` panel adjusts based on the selected section's `type`. I plan to use `lucide-react` for icons and `devicon` for tech stack logos. The stats widget will use the provided GitHub API. Social links will be handled by simple inputs.


**Structuring the Data**

I'm now detailing data structures and utility functions. I'm focusing on defining interfaces for `Section`, `SectionType`, and `SectionData`. I will use a simple utility for array reordering, to keep the core dependency-lite. I'm building out the `generator.ts` file for markdown output and defining the visual logic for `SectionRenderers` and drag-and-drop interactions in `SortableItem`. Finally, I'm working on the `Canvas`, `Sidebar`, and `SettingsPanel` components and the main `App.tsx` layout.


**Refining Component Interactions**

I'm now iterating on the component interactions. I'm focusing on the user interface and user experience, specifically the grid layout to support the sidebar, canvas, and settings. I've designed the canvas as a preview with edit controls, including an empty state. I'm also planning the tabs within the right panel to handle raw markdown and settings. I am ensuring that the `addSection` action will generate unique IDs. I've considered that the github stats and markdown have correct spacing.

entries.description: Root HTML file with Tailwind CSS and Devicon CDN.
TypeScript interfaces for the application state.
Zustand state management for the README sections.
Visual components for the WYSIWYG editor.
Right panel for editing properties and previewing markdown.
Wrapper component for draggable functionality using dnd-kit.
Middle panel where the drag-and-drop editor lives.

It appears the error originates in `components/SettingsPanel.tsx`, specifically with the `import { saveAs } from 'file-saver';` statement. I'm exploring whether the module truly exports `saveAs` or if there's a mismatch in the import statement or the module installation. I've been investigating the `file-saver` module's export, particularly on `esm.sh`. I suspect a mismatch because `esm.sh` typically exports ES modules with default exports. Examining the `esm.sh` link confirms `file-saver` likely uses a default export, not named `saveAs`. The issue is in `components/SettingsPanel.tsx`, where I'm attempting a named import. I need to update the import statement to align with the default export approach or explore alternate import patterns.

I'm now zeroing in on the best way to handle the `file-saver` import in `SettingsPanel.tsx`. The error's clear; I need to change from named import. While it could be either `import saveAs from 'file-saver';` or `import { default as saveAs } from 'file-saver';`, I think a default import is correct, and I'll explore if it needs explicit aliasing due to type definitions. This seems like the most direct fix, despite potential type definition caveats.

**Investigating Extra Spaces**

I'm currently looking into the issue with the "Visitors" badge URL, specifically the added spaces. The problem seems to involve extra characters creeping into the `page_id` parameter, for example, `page_id=ahmetfthmt .ahmetfthmt `. I'm attempting to pinpoint the source of these unwanted spaces to prevent them from rendering. I'll test different scenarios and analyze the code.


**Pinpointing The Source**

I've been examining the generator and renderer components, specifically `utils/generator.ts` and `components/SectionRenderers.tsx`, as they construct the URL for the visitor badge. I'm focusing on how the `username` is handled, and if any unintended characters are introduced during the process. It appears these extra characters are creeping in. I need to trace the data flow through `store/useReadmeStore.ts` to see when and how they are added. I think this will illuminate the source.


**Tracing The Whitespace**

I've determined the issue stems from a trailing space in the `username` variable, leading to the undesirable output. The output format appears to be `${username}.${username}`. I'll need to trim the `username` variable in `utils/generator.ts` and `components/SectionRenderers.tsx` to sanitize the URL and remove the undesirable whitespace. I will also make sure to improve the component's handling of encoding to make it robust. Additionally, I'll focus on a visual fix to ensure proper display of the badge in the canvas.


**Refining The Solution**

I'm now implementing the fix, starting with trimming inputs in `Panel.tsx` and adding `encodeURIComponent` encoding. Trimming input on change appears to be safer for data integrity, I'm verifying this now. I've also added checks to see if `label` includes spaces and will encode those properly. I'll need to trim the `username` in `generator.ts` and `SectionRenderers.tsx`, in both the markdown generator and preview renderer, and then URL-encode parameters. My goal is consistency for the generated output, now.

Ziyaretçi sayacı (Visitor Badge) URL'inde oluşan boşluk sorunu, kullanıcı adının (username) veya etiket (label) metninin URL standartlarına uygun şekilde temizlenmemesi ve encode edilmemesinden kaynaklanıyor. Markdown ve önizleme kısmında bu URL'leri daha güvenli hale getirmek için güncellemeleri yapıyorum.

### Teknik Güncelleme Planı:

1.  **`utils/generator.ts` Güncellemesi:** Üretilen Markdown kodunda `username` alanına `.trim()` uygulanacak ve `label` gibi boşluk içerebilecek alanlar `encodeURIComponent` ile sarmalanacak.
2.  **`components/SectionRenderers.tsx` Güncellemesi:** Önizleme (Canvas) üzerindeki görselin bozulmaması için aynı temizleme mantığı buraya da eklenecek.
3.  **`components/SettingsPanel.tsx` İyileştirmesi:** Veri girişi sırasında boşlukların kullanıcıya hissettirilmeden temizlenmesi için input yönetimi optimize edilecek.

Bu değişiklikler sonucunda `Profile Views` gibi boşluklu metinler `Profile%20Views` olarak işlenecek ve kullanıcı adındaki yanlışlıkla eklenen boşluklar silinecektir.

**Troubleshooting Banner Display**

I'm currently investigating why the banner image (Capsule Render) isn't showing up in the preview. My focus is now on the image rendering process in the `SectionRenderers.tsx` file, where the `bannerUrl` is handled using `img` tags. I'm also reviewing how `HeaderRenderer` processes `title`, `subtitle`, `bannerUrl`, and `showBanner`.


**Analyzing Banner URL**

I've examined the default `bannerUrl`, confirming its validity. I'm now focusing on potential CORS issues, referrer policies, or service availability of `capsule-render.vercel.app`. I'm also checking if CSS, particularly the `opacity-90` class, is affecting the banner's visibility. I want to be certain that the default URL isn't malformed or blocked, and the issue isn't on the API side.


**Refining Banner Display Constraints**

I'm now considering the image rendering constraints. The fixed height (`h-32`) combined with `object-cover` could be cropping the capsule render image, especially given its intended wide aspect ratio. I'm also remembering that `capsule-render` often uses SVGs, which can be problematic if their MIME type isn't correct, or if there are issues with the `Referer` header. The URL is: `https://capsule-render.vercel.app/`.


**Addressing Referrer Policy**

I'm now implementing `referrerPolicy="no-referrer"` on the `img` tag, hoping to resolve the image display. Also, I realized the height constraint (`h-32`) is too restrictive, especially considering the API requests `height=250`. I'll remove the fixed height for now. I am also checking whether the tech stack renderer works the same way. The user said that the image is not appearing. I will try the updates to the referrer policy and height.


**Refining Banner Rendering**

My primary focus is now on the `HeaderRenderer` in `SectionRenderers.tsx`, and I'm updating the component for better banner handling. The URL provided in Markdown is: `![Header](https://capsule-render.vercel.app/api?type=waving&color=gradient&height=250&section=header&text=Hello%20World&fontSize=90)`. I'm removing the restrictive `h-32 object-cover` styles, opting for `w-full h-auto` to accommodate the SVG content. I'm also adding `referrerPolicy="no-referrer"` to all external images in `SectionRenderers.tsx`, especially since GitHub Readme Stats often need this too. I'm double-checking the URL entry is correct, considering the default is stored in the store.


**Implementing Fallback Strategies**

I'm now considering what the user is actually seeing, and it could be a "broken image" icon. I need to make the banner URL check for null or empty strings, and I'll add a fallback image or better styling to handle those scenarios. I'm also remembering that the `utils/generator.ts` file generates stats images, so I'll ensure they use the `referrerPolicy="no-referrer"`. I will apply these fixes.

Görsellerin (özellikle Capsule Render ve GitHub Stats gibi harici API'lerin) önizlemede görünmemesinin en yaygın sebebi, tarayıcının gönderdiği "Referer" başlığının bu servisler tarafından engellenmesi veya yanlış CSS ölçeklendirmesidir.

Aşağıdaki güncellemeler ile:
1.  **`referrerPolicy="no-referrer"`** ekleyerek harici servislerin erişim engellerini aşıyoruz.
2.  **`HeaderRenderer`** içindeki sabit yüksekliği (`h-32`) kaldırıp `h-auto` yaparak banner'ın kesilmeden tam boyut görünmesini sağlıyoruz.
3.  Tüm harici görsellere bu güvenlik/erişim ayarlarını uyguluyoruz.
